explanation: Ono–Swaminathan (arXiv:2509.09553, §1): 'if g(x) is a nonconstant integer-valued polynomial that is eventually positive, then p(g(n)) is even for infinitely many n and odd for infinitely many n'. The formal statement takes g ∈ ℚ[X] of positive degree, integer-valued on ℕ (equivalent to integer-valued on ℤ for polynomials), eventually positive, and uses p(⌊g(n)⌋₊); the floor only matters at the finitely many n where g(n) ≤ 0, so the infinitude claims are unaffected. Faithful.
